title: I Let the Recruiter Keep the Unpaid Task as a Policy

parts.text: I opened the recruiter email and counted eight hours of free work. I am twenty-six, freelance designer, kitchen table, cold tea. The company, Helix, wanted a full brand refresh as a 'quick test.' My name is Lina. The recruiter was Brad, relentlessly upbeat. The brief included a logo, social templates, and a motion draft. I looked at my actual invoice rate on a sticky note, $85. The tea had a film on it because I had forgotten it twice. Brad called. His headset kept clipping. Brad said, "Just do the test and we'll talk numbers" I said, "Numbers first or I don't open Illustrator" The job post had said paid trial. The email did not. I forwarded the post to myself like a superstition. My cat knocked a pen off the table, cheap Bic, blue. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. parts.cliffhanger_hint: He wants a full brand pack tonight, and the posting that promised pay is only in my screenshot.

social.description: Cold tea, an $85 sticky note, and a recruiter headset that clipped. The posting said paid. Would you have opened Illustrator?

parts.text: I sent a one-page estimate instead of a logo. Brad replied that estimates kill momentum. I posted the anonymized brief on a freelance board with the pay-test screenshot. Three designers said Helix had run this trick all quarter. A woman named Keisha had already done the motion draft for free. She emailed Brad and cc'd a Helix HR alias she found on their site. I joined the cc. The table still had the tea film. HR asked if the trial was approved. Brad's upbeat died in writing. HR said, "Was this trial authorized" Brad said, "It was exploratory" They posted a real paid trial two weeks later, $400, still low. I declined. Keisha took it and got the job, which I cheered. I bought new tea and a better pen. Momentum, it turns out, is just unpaid labor with a headset. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there.
